analysis.title: China: Exports moderated, while imports surged in October
key_insights: China's October nominal exports fell 1.0% m/m sa after a 6.5% jump in September, leaving annual growth at 35.2% oya (market consensus 36.3%, JPM 32.4%).
The export pullback was concentrated in the EU (-3.5% m/m sa), Russia (-5.0%) and Africa (-6.5%), partly offset by Latin America (+4.2%).

Product performance on exports was mixed: ADP exports rose 5.4% m/m sa, integrated circuits fell 2.7%, mobile phones fell 2.8%, autos fell 1.1% after an 8.0% surge in September, and low-end consumer goods fell 4.1%, partly unwinding holiday-related restocking.
Imports rose 6.5% m/m sa to 41.6% oya, well above market consensus of 33.9% and JPM's 30.1%, driven by a rebound in energy import volumes and tech supply-chain demand.

Energy imports: crude oil volumes rose 4.6% m/m sa, refined oil products rose 74.0% and coal rose 9.9% on winter restocking. High-tech imports rose 2.5%, a 12th consecutive month of sequential expansion.

The trade surplus narrowed to US$105.3bn in October from a record $133.5bn in September. Year-to-date surplus is US$1043bn, putting the full-year surplus on track for about $1.3tr versus $1.2tr last year.
Global commodity prices rallied and unit prices for integrated circuits and mobile phones continued to rise, consistent with the strong October PPI. Consumer goods prices stayed sluggish.

JPM expects auto exports to support export growth through year-end, as Chinese automakers may accelerate hybrid EV deliveries to the EU before proposed import restrictions. Support should come from volumes rather than prices given weak domestic demand and excess production.

Crude oil import volumes are likely to recover further as Middle Eastern supply and pricing normalize and refiners rebuild inventories, but the rebound should stay moderate given weak domestic fuel demand.

Global tech prices should keep supporting both nominal exports and imports, so the net effect on the trade balance is uncertain. A gradual moderation in commodity prices should weigh on headline import growth even if import volumes stay firm.

US midterm elections add uncertainty. Tighter restrictions on US data-center development could slow AI investment and weigh on China's exports of data-center equipment such as power equipment, batteries and optical components. JPM sees the impact as more medium-term because much of the 2027 capex pipeline is already built or funded, and China's direct exposure to US AI demand is smaller than Korea's and Taiwan's.

JPM's overall view is that China's trade outlook remains resilient, supported by global demand, manufacturing competitiveness, market diversification and the AI investment cycle, despite trade barriers and CNY appreciation pressure. Strong imports do not necessarily signal a broad recovery in domestic demand.

sector_views.rationale: Auto exports should remain a support to export growth through year-end as automakers may bring forward hybrid EV deliveries to the EU ahead of proposed import restrictions.
Sustained AI-related demand supports tech prices and China's high-tech imports and exports, though the net effect on the trade balance is uncertain.

risk_factors: Tighter US data-center restrictions after the midterm elections could slow AI investment and weigh on China's exports of data-center-related equipment.
Rising trade barriers, including proposed EU import restrictions on Chinese hybrid EVs, and CNY appreciation pressure.
Moderating global commodity and oil prices could soften headline import growth.
Weak domestic demand, excess production and weak domestic fuel demand limit price support and the pace of the import rebound.
geopolitical: Proposed EU import restrictions on Chinese hybrid EVs may prompt Chinese automakers to accelerate deliveries before they take effect.
Growing protectionist pressure in other markets could reinforce the incentive to bring forward auto shipments.
US midterm elections could bring tighter restrictions on US data-center development, with potential spillover to China's exports of data-center-related equipment.
Middle Eastern supply and pricing normalization is expected to support a recovery in China's crude oil import volumes.

tension_points.bull_case: Supportive global demand, manufacturing competitiveness, market diversification and the AI investment cycle should continue to underpin exports, and auto exports may be front-loaded ahead of EU restrictions.
tension_points.bear_case: Rising trade barriers, CNY appreciation pressure, and possible tighter US data-center restrictions could weigh on exports of data-center-related equipment.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Tighter US data-center restrictions after the midterms that slow AI investment, though JPM sees the impact as medium-term since much of the 2027 capex pipeline is already under construction or funded.

theme_stances.key_argument: Supportive global demand, manufacturing competitiveness, export-market diversification and the AI investment cycle should continue to underpin exports.
